box: Box E -- the 'no motion' claim. love-match.ts is claimed to contain no .animate(, matchMedia, requestAnimationFrame, or timer, so there is nothing for a reduced-motion guard to suppress. Verified rather than trusted: document.getAnimations() and a computed-style scan of every node under #stage for a non-'none' animation-name or a nonzero transition-duration, both with reduced motion emulated and with it allowed, on the pick screen and the result screen.
method: Two separate real headless Chrome launches, per docs/agents/browser-verification.md's --force-prefers-reduced-motion recipe: the existing instance on :9222 (no flag = 'normal') and a second instance on :9223 with --force-prefers-reduced-motion --user-data-dir=/tmp/cdp-prof-lm-rm. Same box-e.mjs script run against both via CDP_PORT=9222 / CDP_PORT=9223 (scripts/driver.mjs reads CDP_PORT from the environment). Calibrated the emulation flag itself both ways in-page (matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches): false on :9222, true on :9223 -- the flag is confirmed to have actually flipped runtime behaviour, not just been passed on the command line. The scan (`animationName.split(',')` and `transitionDuration.split(',').map(parseFloat)`, taking the max across every comma-separated value, per the trap that '0s, 0.3s' is not caught by a naive first-value check) walked the stage element itself plus every descendant, on both the pick screen (2-person roster, ก้อง/ฟ้า, added via named-entry) and the result screen (after picking ก้อง then ฟ้า), in both Chrome instances -- four scans total.
capturedAtCommitNote: Working tree is dirty at capture time; this walk verifies uncommitted work, not a clean HEAD. git status --short showed: ' M src/games/manifest.ts', '?? public/og/love-match.png', '?? src/games/love-match.test.mjs', '?? src/games/love-match.ts'. The capture reflects the tree as it stood at run time.
reducedMotionSuppressionVerdict: N/A -- there is no animation or transition anywhere under #stage in either state, so there is nothing for a suppression guard to suppress. Per docs/agents/browser-verification.md this is recorded as N/A, not as a passing suppression check.
